verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four cases have the failure measurement dated before the bearing was fitted: the Bexley lathe was 'fitted 4 May' but 'ran 340 hours longer before failure by 27 March', and the Corbin conveyor was 'fitted 2 August' but measured 'by 21 July'. The other two cases (9 January to 24 February, 6 October to 25 November) run about seven weeks forward, so these two readings cannot postdate installation.

A named alternative cause reaches every plot: 'Rainfall in each plot's season was the highest on record, roughly double the year before,' and 'every plot stood in the open, watered by rain alone.' Since the comparison is against the previous summer, the doubled rainfall alone can account for the 8-13 cm of extra height.

Cohorts one and three are measured before the email went out: Norway signups were 'emailed 24 March' yet retention is read 'by 9 March', and Vietnam signups were 'emailed 25 October' yet read 'by 10 October' - fifteen days earlier in both cases, while cohorts two and four run 24 days forward. Week-two retention cannot be observed before the intervention.

The timing average is computed on a self-selected subset: 'Timings cover the runs that reported a finish time, and about a sixth of each depot's runs reported none.' Roughly 17 percent of runs are dropped, and runs that fail to log a finish are plausibly the delayed ones, which is enough to produce the 5-9 minute improvement on its own.
